lead.label: 6a
lead.why: Abstract names two potent BET inhibitors, 3a and 6a; 6a is the one taken into the in vivo pharmacokinetic and metabolic-stability studies ('excellent brain penetration') and is called '[18F]6a is a potential PET radiotracer'. The cold (non-radioactive) 6a is the compound transcribed; its 18F radiolabelling (Scheme 2) is not transcribed.

reactions.conditions: p-TSA (cat.), CHCl3, diol added (the text says dropwise addition of the acid solution to the diol solution to reduce dimerisation); Scheme 1 says 50 C, 24 h, procedure says rt overnight; 55.1% (5a)
reactions.source: Results/Chemistry, Scheme 1 step a; Experimental 'General Procedure for Synthesis of Intermediates 2a-e and 5a-c'; 5a entry

reactions.conditions: DAST (10 equiv), CH2Cl2, -78 C to rt, overnight; 56.1% (6a)
reactions.source: Scheme 1 step c; Experimental 'General Procedure for Synthesis of 3a-e and 6a-c'; 6a entry

notes: No SI file. Two-step route from commercial (+)-JQ1 carboxylic acid. 3a (2-fluoroethyl ester, also named in the abstract) would be the same chemistry with ethylene glycol. Stereocentre (S) as stated; SMILES chirality tag is copied from the PubChem-style SMILES of (+)-JQ1 acid and should be checked as S by the OPSIN comparison. The paper's 3d entry is mislabelled '2-Fluoroethyl' (typo), irrelevant for 6a. Step 1 temperature differs between Scheme 1 (50 C, 24 h) and the experimental text (rt, overnight); the DAST equivalents are 10 (0.33 mL, 2.5 mmol per 0.25 mmol).
